title: FAKE-01 referral letter (cardiology)

pages.text:
SYNTHETIC / FAKE TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL PATIENT — FOR SOFTWARE DEMONSTRATION ONLY

Maple Test Family Health Team (FAKE)

100 Example Road, Suite 1, Testville ON  Z9Z 9Z9 · Tel 555-0100 · Fax 555-0101

October 2, 2026

Dr. Ian Sampleton
Cardiology Clinic, Lakeview Test General Hospital (FAKE)

Re: Rowan Testwood · DOB: 21 June 1958 · Health card: TEST-0000-0000 (FAKE)

Dear Dr. Sampleton,

Thank you for seeing Mr. Testwood, a 68-year-old retired electrician, for assessment of exertional chest pressure. Over the past six weeks he has had central chest tightness when walking uphill or carrying groceries. It lasts 3 to 5 minutes and settles with rest. Twice it came with shortness of breath. He has had no pain at rest, no fainting and no palpitations.

Background

- Type 2 diabetes for 12 years (last HbA1c 7.9% in June 2026)

- Hypertension, on treatment

- Dyslipidemia

- Former smoker: 30 pack-years, quit in 2015

- Father had a myocardial infarction at 61

Current medications

- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily

- Glyburide 5 mg twice daily

- Ramipril 5 mg daily

- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily

- Acetylsalicylic acid 81 mg daily, started on 28 September 2026

Allergies: penicillin (rash).

Examination and investigations

BP 148/88, heart rate 78 and regular, BMI 31. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Chest clear. No ankle swelling.

Resting ECG (30 September 2026): sinus rhythm, 0.5 mm ST depression in V4 to V6. There is no earlier ECG to compare.

Bloods (25 September 2026): creatinine 98 µmol/L (eGFR 68), LDL cholesterol 3.1 mmol/L, hemoglobin 138 g/L.

Questions

1. Is this stable angina, and does he need an exercise test or a coronary angiogram?

2. Should his statin dose be increased, and what LDL target do you suggest?

3. Would you recommend an SGLT2 inhibitor instead of glyburide, given his heart risk?

I have given him a nitroglycerin spray and asked him to call 911 if the pain lasts more than 10 minutes or comes at rest. I would be grateful if he could be seen within the next 2 to 4 weeks.

Sincerely,

Dr. Henrietta Fakeham, MD (FAKE)
Family Physician, Maple Test Family Health Team

cc: Rowan Testwood (patient copy)
